domain.value: masked video autoencoder (ViT encoder + shallow decoder predicting normalized pixels of masked space-time cubes; MSE in pixel space), self-supervised on general human-action video (Kinetics-400 / Something-Something V2)

quotes.quote: VideoMAE is an extension of [Masked Autoencoders (MAE)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06377) to video. The architecture of the model is very similar to that of a standard Vision Transformer (ViT), with a decoder on top for predicting pixel values for masked patches.
The loss function is mean squared error (MSE) loss between the normalized masked tokens and reconstructed ones in the pixel space
Figure 1: VideoMAE performs the task of masking random cubes and reconstructing the missing ones with an asymmetric encoder-decoder architecture.
VideoMAE model pre-trained on Kinetics-400 for 1600 epochs in a self-supervised way.

architecture.type: vanilla ViT (joint space-time attention) encoder on 2x16x16 cube tokens, tube masking 90%; 4-layer (ViT-B) / 12-layer (ViT-L) decoder for pixel reconstruction (pretraining only)
architecture.representation: encoder output tokens (768-dim per cube for ViT-B, 1024 for ViT-L) or their mean / [CLS]-style pooled vector; decoder not needed for features

pretraining_data.summary: Each released checkpoint is pre-trained on ONE named public benchmark, without labels: Kinetics-400 (~240k 10-s YouTube clips, 400 human-action classes) for videomae-base/-large/-base-short; Something-Something V2 (~169k crowd-sourced clips, 174 motion-centric classes) for videomae-base-ssv2; UCF101 for one Google-Drive checkpoint. No extra data ('no external data').

Here models are self-supervised pre-trained with a masking ratio of 90% for 1600 epochs on Kinetics-400.

The Kinetics-400 contains around 240k training videos and 20k validation videos of 10s from 400 classes. The Something-Something V2 is another large-scale video dataset, having around 169k videos for training and 20k videos for validation. In contrast to Kinetics-400, this dataset contains 174 motion-centric action classes.
The dataset contains 400 human action classes, with at least 400 video clips for each action. Each clip lasts around 10s and is taken from a different YouTube video.
The database currently contains more than 100,000 videos across 174 classes, which are defined as caption-templates. We also describe the challenges in crowd-sourcing this data at scale.

VideoMAE is an extension of [Masked Autoencoders (MAE)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06377) to video. The architecture of the model is very similar to that of a standard Vision Transformer (ViT), with a decoder on top for predicting pixel values for masked patches.
One typically places a linear layer on top of the [CLS] token, as the last hidden state of this token can be seen as a representation of an entire video.
The loss function is mean squared error (MSE) loss between the normalized masked tokens and reconstructed ones in the pixel space
Figure 1: VideoMAE performs the task of masking random cubes and reconstructing the missing ones with an asymmetric encoder-decoder architecture.

Here models are self-supervised pre-trained with a masking ratio of 90% for 1600 epochs on Kinetics-400.

The Kinetics-400 contains around 240k training videos and 20k validation videos of 10s from 400 classes. The Something-Something V2 is another large-scale video dataset, having around 169k videos for training and 20k videos for validation. In contrast to Kinetics-400, this dataset contains 174 motion-centric action classes.
The dataset contains 400 human action classes, with at least 400 video clips for each action. Each clip lasts around 10s and is taken from a different YouTube video.
The database currently contains more than 100,000 videos across 174 classes, which are defined as caption-templates. We also describe the challenges in crowd-sourcing this data at scale.
In experiments, the stride τ is set to 4 and 2 on Kinetics and Something-Something, respectively.
